abstract: Dynamic F-actin networks regulate intracellular vesicular transport and membrane morphogenesis for cell development. However, the molecular mechanisms through which membrane-associated F-actin actively drives these processes remain elusive. Here, we uncover that F-actin associates with spherical vacuole (SV) to form a "ring-encircling-sphere" (RCS) structure, which guides homotypic fusion of SVs to central vacuoles (CVs) during plant development. We found that the SV-encircling F-actin scaffolded the spatial proximity between SVs and CVs, thus facilitating vacuolar homotypic fusion, while the F-actin crosslinker STOMATAL CLOSURE-RELATED ACTIN-BINDING PROTEIN 1 (SCAB1) enabled these dynamic interplays. In SCAB1-deficient mutants, the RCS tethering is markedly impaired, leading to disrupted vacuolar morphogenesis and abnormal cell development. An additional in vitro F-actin-vesicle reconstitution system further supported the scaffolding function of SCAB1 in coupling F-actin-bound vesicles. Together, these results reveal that actin-mediated spatial organization governs vacuolar fusion and identify a mechanism by which cytoskeletal geometry controls organelle morphogenesis.
